# sigma_smtp_settings (Resource)

Singleton resource managing the organization's custom SMTP server for outbound email. Destroying it deletes the SMTP settings. The password is write-only: Sigma never returns it, so changes made outside Terraform to the password are not detected.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sigma_smtp_settings" "main" {
  host         = "smtp.example.com"
  port         = "587"
  username     = "sigma-mailer"
  password     = var.smtp_password
  sender_email = "no-reply@example.com"
  sender_name  = "Sigma"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) SMTP server hostname.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) SMTP password. Never read back from Sigma.
- `port` (String) SMTP server port, as a string.
- `sender_email` (String) Address emails are sent from.
- `username` (String) SMTP username.

### Optional

- `global_bcc_addresses` (List of String) Addresses BCC'd on every outbound email.
- `reply_to_address` (String) Reply-to address for outbound email.
- `sender_name` (String) Display name emails are sent from.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Singleton. The password is not imported: set it in config and the next apply writes it.
terraform import sigma_smtp_settings.example smtp
```
